what: First launch after sign-in: link where you sell, each site on its own and each optional; an optional saved pickup spot; then a photo of the first thing. Three short steps to a first listing.

frame.who: A new person, signed in a minute ago, with nothing linked or listed (world new); most often the person clearing out.
frame.how_often: Once, and again only after signing out.
frame.came_to: Get the first thing listed with the least setup.
frame.costly_mistake: A step that blocks: a site that will not sign in, or a question that could wait. Every site can be skipped, a failed sign-in says why and offers Retry, and Continue never waits for all five.
frame.ways_out: Skip for now with nothing linked; Skip on the pickup step with no spot; Later on the photo step goes to Today; a site's 2FA or captcha shows its own step, and a timeout gives Retry (spec/ways-out.md).
frame.in_the_loop: The person signs in on the site's own page; the password never reaches secondhand, and the page says so.

back: The sign-in step has no Back and cannot be skipped. The address and code steps go back to the choices. The sites step has no Back: it is the first screen after sign-in. The pickup step goes back to the sites step, and the photo step to the pickup step.
decisions: Three steps, not the seven in spec/pages.md §6.1: sign-in is already done, and email for sales and alerts are asked the first time each is needed, so nothing stands between a new person and a first listing (the brief: the fewest steps to the first listing).

An optional saved pickup spot is the only pickup step (spec/edge-cases.md §16; decision: no fixed pickup windows): no hours to set and no calendar read. Days and times are tapped when a buyer wants to meet, so the step asks one thing and can be skipped.

The spot is a blank field, A public place, with one line on where is safest (a police station's safe exchange zone, then a busy, lit store entrance); the address goes out only on its own tap later. A map of safe spots needs place data the demo does not have.
No carousel and no promises: the first screen is the first task.
The wordmark sits in the nav on the first step, which is the first screen a new person sees after sign-in; the photo step has Back instead.

Every site has its own state and act, and Continue works with none linked (Ben, 03:22). With none linked the foot reads Skip for now in gray; with one it reads Continue in black, so the black pill appears once there is something to continue with.
The import of found listings is left to Today as merge cards, so linking never waits on a scan.
Mercari's first Link in the demo times out at the code step, so the failed state and Retry can be seen.

?state= draws each state of the first step: typical with one site linked, loading with one signing in, failed with Mercari's try timed out, offline with Waiting for signal. Empty, one and dense are skipped: first launch is only for a new person.

Sign-in comes first and cannot be skipped (spec/features/connect.md, Signing in to secondhand). The 6-second hero loop is left for later (TODO in onboarding.tsx, spec/pages.md §6.1). The app has no client for /v1/auth yet, so the demo drives it: Apple and Google succeed after a short wait, and the email code accepts any 6 digits except 000000, which fails. ?signed=1 skips sign-in, and states typical, one, dense and empty imply a signed-in person.
